task: Research: open-source rigging/animation/mocap tooling + AI failure modes + Prisma 3D co-authoring
resume_brief: STANDALONE BRIEF — two-track research, owner-directed 2026-10-09. CONTEXT: We're building promo/entrance videos for game characters (Bannon repo). Our pipeline hit hard limits: auto-weighted GLB shoulders web/tear past 15deg arm raise (measured), hand-keyed taunts instead of mocap, no corrective shapes, no twist bones. The owner (an experienced builder) called out that real studios hand-paint weights, use twist joints, corrective blendshapes, dual-quaternion skinning — and that I keep hand-rolling scripts instead of bringing in open-source tools. TRACK 1 — OPEN-SOURCE TOOLING LANDSCAPE: survey everything open-source we should wire into our character pipeline: auto-rigging (Rigify, Auto-Rig Pro alternatives, Mixamo rigging API), weight-painting aids, corrective-shape/deformation tools (Blender Corrective Smooth and beyond), mocap sources (CMU database, Mixamo free animations, DeepMotion/Rokoko free tiers, phone-based mocap), retargeting tools (Blender retargeting addons, Rokoko Studio free), muscle/deformation systems. For each: what it does, license, how it fits OUR pipeline (Blender 4.0.2 headless + GLB + game harness), and a concrete wire-up recommendation. Prioritize tools that fix OUR measured problems: shoulder deformation, taunt-quality motion, mocap retargeting. TRACK 2 — AI FAILURE MODES: research why AI agents fail at 3D production work like this — the known failure patterns (accepting own subagent claims without verification, procedural fakery vs real data, reinventing tools, confident misreporting), and what guardrails actually work (verification laws, evidence requirements, tool-first policies). Be concrete and practical, not philosophical — the output should make our pipeline harder to fool. OUTPUT: a research report at ~/workspace/bannon-video-pipe/docs/AI_RIGGING_RESEARCH.md covering both tracks with specific wire-up recommendations ranked by impact. RULES: heartbeat THIS checkpoint every 15 min; real sources only (link everything); no invented tools — verify each one exists. When done mark checkpoint done and report the top 5 wire-up recommendations.
